item.text: {"question_id":"3B.2","answer":"No. For 2023, the evidence shows formal prevention and disciplinary capacity but not reliable operational control. Egypt reported 47 Interior Ministry human-rights courses through June, 29 anti-trafficking courses for 577 staff, and disciplinary or legal measures involving 769 Interior Ministry employees through May; however, 380 findings included cruelty, unlawful detention, ill-treatment, torture, and excessive force, while 363 cases were suspended and 22 remained pending, so the figures do not demonstrate deterrence or senior accountability. Continuing state-custody deaths, arbitrary and prolonged detention, and reported torture or ill-treatment further indicate unresolved abuse. The government also reported strong counterterrorism capacity and sharply reduced Sinai violence in 2023, but casualty and outcome data were difficult to verify under restricted reporting, and terrorism authorities continued to be used against activists and critics. Historical evidence that the military recruited, armed, paid, and directed North Sinai militias, found no accountability for abusive members, and that Sisi ordered commanders to use “all brute force” establishes important institutional and policy context, but does not by itself prove a direct 2023 order or nationwide attribution. The best-supported conclusion is recurring, state-attributed or institutionally tolerated abuse alongside partial formal safeguards and some security gains, rather than demonstrated preventive control.","supporting_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0023-E014","BATCH-0023-E015","BATCH-0023-E017","BATCH-0006-E009"],"contrary_or_qualifying_evidence_ids":["BATCH-0006-E010","BATCH-0006-E018","BATCH-0006-E023","BATCH-0002-E016"],"limitations_and_gaps":["The disciplinary and training figures are government-reported; reduced terrorist activity does not establish lawful restraint."],"corrections_made":["Qualified the favorable training and disciplinary evidence by stating that 363 cases were suspended and 22 remained pending, and that the figures do not demonstrate deterrence.","Added the continuing 2023 evidence on state-custody deaths, detention, torture, ill-treatment, and use of counterterrorism authorities against critics.","Separated historical militia recruitment, arming, payment, direction, and the “all brute force” directive from direct 2023 operational evidence.","Reframed the conclusion as partial formal safeguards and some security gains coexisting with recurring or institutionally tolerated abuse, without claiming every local act or a direct 2023 order is personally attributable."],"reasons_to_reopen_full_ledger":["A complete 2023 command, appointment, resourcing, and disciplinary ledger could clarify senior responsibility and whether historical security practices continued operationally.","Independent case-level verification of the reported disciplinary outcomes and 2023 prison deaths could materially change the assessment of accountability and remedy."]}
